jobs.description:
At KMD, we build digital solutions used by millions of people around the world. These solutions are the digital foundations of our most important institutions, from governments and public services to financial industries and private companies. Our mission is to ensure that they are reliable, accessible, and efficient.

We believe that the future is what you make it. So a career at KMD is a career with purpose and freedom. One where you’ll have a direct hand in improving the lives of people, while being empowered with the resources and autonomy to shape the course of your own professional journey.

As part of our strategy, centralizing commercials and our work in the partner environment is essential to ensure best in class solutions, and a key factor is our collaboration across the organization. You will play the key role in this.

About the job

Are you someone who takes ownership, creates momentum and enjoys turning ideas into action?

We are looking for a Partner Manager to join our Bid Excellence area. What matters to us is your ability to drive, collaborate and execute on our partner strategy.

You will work closely with the leadership of Bid Excellence and collaborate with senior stakeholders across KMD. This is a role for someone who enjoys taking initiative, navigating different stakeholders and contribute with positive energy and a pragmatic approach.

What you will be doing

As our new Partner Manager, you will be part of Bid Excellence and work closely with the leadership team.

Your role will require you to take ownership of assignments, move activities forward and work collaboratively across the organization. You will have a close collaboration with your manager, who will be your main point of reference, while your work may also involve supporting and interacting with senior stakeholders across KMD.

The role offers an opportunity to develop your experience in a highly collaborative environment where initiative, curiosity and execution matter.

Responsibilities

You will:

• Take ownership of driving the execution of partnerships

• Establish a clear framework for go-to-market collaboration, ensuring that agreements and decisions are translated into action.

• Act as the central interface between internal and external stakeholders

• Strengthen relationships, activate connections across the organization, and connect opportunities with the relevant decision-makers, capabilities, and solutions.

• Establish a clear cadence for tracking progress, priorities, risks, and decision requirements, while ensuring the right information is available and the relevant stakeholders are involved at the right time.

• Identify tangible growth opportunities through customer, partner, and market insights, and use these insights to drive the development and execution of KMD's international strategy.

You are

We imagine that you are someone who enjoys making things happen and collaborating across different areas.

You:

• Have a proactive and hands-on approach.

• Take ownership and follow things through.

• Enjoy collaborating with others.

• Are comfortable working with different stakeholders.

• Can communicate confidently with senior stakeholders.

• Bring positive energy to the people around you.

• Are pragmatic and focused on finding solutions.

• Can work independently while knowing when to involve others.

Most importantly, you have a “get things done” mindset and enjoy working in an environment where collaboration matters.

Life at KMD

At KMD, we build digital solutions used by millions of people around the world. Our solutions form part of the digital foundation of important institutions, ranging from governments and public services to financial industries and private companies.

Our workplace reflects our values, and we work to create a welcoming and inclusive environment where everyone can be themselves. Well-being and autonomy are important to us, and we want our employees to have the opportunity to shape their own professional journey.

**Job Description

**Are you dedicated to building robust, innovative solutions and motivated to assist in shaping the future of modern banking? _Then join our Customer Relationship squad at Danske Bank!

_The Customer Relationship squad is responsible for the data and core capabilities of the relationship between a customer and subsidiaries of the Danske Bank Group.

You will work closely with the team and the Product Owner to align with stakeholders and ensure a seamless customer journey, and you will be part of a modernization at the very core of the bank.

We are looking for a Senior Java Software Engineer who enjoys translating business needs into scalable and secure technical solutions. As a squad, we are exploring how AI agents and tools can enhance our development processes, ways of working and the value we deliver. You will help shape this journey by turning promising ideas into practical improvements for the team.

Working closely with your colleagues, you will contribute throughout the development lifecycle – from understanding and refining requirements to implementation, testing, deployment and ongoing support – with efficiency and quality at the heart of everything we do.

**You will

**

• Contribute to solutions throughout the development lifecycle, from design and implementation to deployment and handover to end users.

• Apply your experience to solve complex technical challenges, share knowledge and support colleagues in delivering strong outcomes.

• Ensure high-quality code by applying sound engineering practices and writing automated tests.

• Help us move towards event- and API-focused, cloud-hosted solutions where data consumer self-service is the way forward.

• Operate within a self-organising Scrum team, applying an agile mindset.

• Support, maintain and modernise existing solutions.

• Use AI-assisted development tools to improve productivity and quality and help the team explore and adopt valuable AI solutions.

**What We Are Looking For

**

• Strong proficiency in Java and its supporting development tools.

• Hands-on experience designing, developing and testing modern software solutions; experience with cloud-native systems is an advantage.

• Professional English communication skills.

• A proactive and collaborative approach to working within and across teams.

• An interest in improving engineering practices and sharing knowledge with colleagues.

• Good understanding of DevOps and CI/CD tools, such as Azure DevOps, GitHub Actions or Jenkins.

• Hands-on experience using AI as part of software development and a strong focus on identifying, testing and championing AI solutions within the team

• A team-oriented mindset and the ability to communicate clearly about technical decisions and solutions.

**Your Benefits

**As a modern workplace, we offer our employees a canteen, rooftop terrace, regular social and professional events, a very attractive benefits package including health and accident insurance, pension, and many other perks. You will also get 6 weeks of vacation and 5 extra care days annually and be part of a flexible work environment. We expect you to be working minimum 3-4 days per week from our office in Copenhagen.

**Sounds interesting?

**We will start conducting interviews in November, and application deadline is Monday 9th of November. If you have any questions or would like more information about the role, you are welcome to contact IT Chapter Lead Brian Skou Hansen at briah@danskebank.dk.

**About Us

**Danske Bank is a Nordic bank with bridges to the world around us. For 150 years, we have supported people and businesses in releasing their potential. A career with us is an opportunity to join a community of 22,000 colleagues in a culture where we are committed to Teaming Up, Owning It and Being Open. Together, we are on a journey to transform Danske Bank into a better bank. For our customers, our employees and the societies around us.

Build Intelligent Systems That Create Real Impact

Are you motivated by solving complex problems with data and AI?

Do you enjoy transforming business challenges into scalable, production-ready solutions?

At VENZO, we’re expanding our Data & AI team and are looking for experienced profiles across mid-to-senior level — from strong hands-on engineers to technical leaders who can shape architecture and guide others.

If you want your work to move beyond experimentation and into real-world implementation, this could be the right place for you.

About VENZO

At VENZO, we believe in the power of technology to create meaningful change – today, not tomorrow.

You’ll join a team of specialists who live and breathe digital transformation, helping some of Denmark’s largest and most influential organizations turn data into action. Here, innovation isn’t a buzzword – it’s how we think, collaborate, and deliver.

About the Role

You will contribute directly to the design, development, and deployment of advanced data and AI systems in cloud-based environments.

Your responsibilities may include:

• Architecting and implementing end-to-end AI and machine learning solutions

• Deploying, monitoring, and optimizing models on cloud platforms

• Translating business requirements into structured technical solutions

• Ensuring solutions are maintainable, scalable, and aligned with best practices

• Evaluating and applying emerging technologies within AI and GenAI

For more senior candidates, the role also includes:

• Defining technical direction and architectural standards

• Acting as a primary technical contact for clients

• Leading workstreams and mentoring team members

• Contributing to the evolution of our Data & AI capabilities and service offerings

We value profiles who can combine deep technical execution with sound judgment in real client environments.

Your Background

We are open to different experience levels, provided you bring strong fundamentals and practical experience.

Experience and Education

• Degree in Computer Science, Engineering, Mathematics, or equivalent practical experience

• 2+ years of experience in data engineering or AI/ML, delivering production-ready solutions

• Hands-on experience across the full ML lifecycle — from experimentation to deployment and monitoring

• Experience with generative AI

• For senior profiles: experience leading technical initiatives or mentoring others

Technical Capabilities

You have experience working within modern data and AI ecosystems, including:

• Programming: Python and SQL, Typescript is a plus

• Cloud: Microsoft Azure (e.g., Azure ML, Data Factory) or other cloud plattforms

• Databricks (Spark, Delta Lake, MLflow)

• Machine Learning: Classical ML techniques and generative AI applications

• GenAI Tooling: LLM APIs, prompt engineering, RAG patterns, frameworks such as LangChain or Microsoft Agent Framework

• MLOps: CI/CD, model lifecycle management, orchestration tools, version control

• Data Engineering: ETL processes and large-scale data processing

How You Work

• Analytical and structured in your problem-solving approach

• Comfortable operating in client-facing environments

• Able to communicate complex technical topics in business-relevant terms

• Pragmatic, quality-driven, and accountable for outcomes

What You Can Expect From Us

• Meaningful, technically challenging projects with real business visibility

• A strong professional environment with high standards and high trust

• Autonomy in how you structure and deliver your work

• Access to modern tooling, platforms, and certifications (including Microsoft)

• Competitive compensation and comprehensive benefits

• Continuous development — technically and professionally

Let’s Talk

Send your CV or a short introduction to hr@venzo.com.

We’re happy to meet for a coffee and explore whether there’s a mutual fit.

At a big company, the platform layer is a hundred engineers, and you own a slice of it. A driver. A subsystem. A corner of the release pipeline. You go deep, but you rarely get to hold the whole thing. With us you will. One team owns the entire layer: the operating system and firmware on every Airtame, the streaming stack underneath it, the releases that reach devices in the field, and the work of turning new hardware into a shipping product.

The role is roughly 60% hands-on the hardest problems and 40% growing the engineers who work on them.

**About Airtame

**We're around 55 people, headquartered in Copenhagen, and you'd work from there or remotely from within the EU. We make the hardware and the software that runs on it, so a change you make to the firmware ships to every Airtame in the field. The team is cross-functional and spread across Europe, and it reaches a global market from a small base.

Year one outcomes

Take AirPlay and Miracast from beta to default. They're in beta today. A year from now they should be solid enough to ship on by default across the Airtame product line, so customers get them without opting in and never have to think about which protocol they're using. Judge it by connection success rates on the fleet, and by how many customers rely on them day to day.

Make firmware releases boring. The best release is the one nobody has to think about: a predictable cadence, an automated quality bar, and shipping to the whole fleet as routine. A year from now, cutting a release should be a low-drama process the team trusts, and that should let you ship improvements more often. Judge it by release frequency, and by the confidence behind each one.

Turn the next board into a shipping Airtame. New silicon has to boot, hold a network, manage its heat, and run conferencing well enough to sell. By year-end there's a repeatable path from a board landing on a desk to a build QA can test, and you own it. Judge it by how long that path takes, and whether the thermal and acoustic targets hold.

Lead the team. You'll run the 1:1s, set the technical bar, and support team members' growth. The measure is simple: a year in, the team runs on your leadership day to day.

Push AI-assisted development further. The team already builds with AI daily. You'll lead the next step: sharper workflows, better tooling choices, new patterns that make the whole group faster. By year-end, the team's AI practices should be visibly ahead of where they started.

Who you are

• The player-coach. You've set a team's technical direction: the architecture calls, the reviews where the hard problems get caught. And you want the people side too. Growing engineers, running 1:1s, hiring. You're not looking to trade one for the other. Maybe you've been a staff engineer or tech lead ready to own a team, or a manager who never stopped writing code. Either way, 60/40 sounds about right to you.

• At home where software meets hardware. Embedded Linux is your familiar ground: the kernel, the BSP, userspace, C and C++ running on the device itself. You've spent time close to the metal: wireless stacks, streaming protocols, drivers. You can reason about a bug whether it lives in the firmware, the network, or the silicon.

• You ship to hardware you can't reach. When it's firmware on a device mounted in someone's meeting room, a bad release doesn't just roll back with a hotfix. You've owned software that ships to the field, so staged rollouts, over-the-air updates, and testing on the devices themselves come naturally. "Works on my bench" isn't the finish line for you.

• You've turned new hardware into a product. Bare silicon arrives, and someone has to make it boot, talk to the network, manage its heat, and eventually stream. You've done that kind of bringup, or worked close enough to it to lead the people who do.

• You use AI as a daily tool. You write code with it, debug with it, prototype with it. You've formed your own view on where it speeds things up and where it gets in the way, and you help the people around you do the same.

**Logistics

**Location: Remote in Europe, or hybrid from our Copenhagen office.

Employment type: Full-time preferred. We're also open to a project-based contract scoped to delivering the native protocol implementations.

****Why Airtame:

• A shift worth architecting. Airtame's software is moving onto a widening range of devices, including hardware from partners. Leading Platform now means designing for that spread, a bigger and more open problem than keeping one hardware line running.

• A span you can hold. From the bootloader to the release that reaches the field, the whole layer is one person's to shape here, at a size where you can still keep it in your head.

• A healthy work-life balance.

• Significant responsibility and ownership over projects and your field of expertise.

• Five weeks paid vacation and 5 days of extra paid AirtameFlex days.

• Flexible work environment, with a hybrid mindset.

• Pension and private health insurance (on FTE Copenhagen contract).

Airtame is an equal opportunity employer. We have colleagues across the globe, with both in-office and full-time remote workers. This feeds into our international hybrid mindset, with people from 25+ nationalities that make up the Airtame team.

Our work-life cultural balance is key to our success. Our team encompasses our values of trust and open communication to support each other and to collaborate in a fun and collective way.

Most companies that do conferencing hand you one slice of it. The desktop app, or the media pipeline, or, maybe, the join flow. Everything else you pass over a wall to another team. Not in this case. One team owns the whole path across the Airtame platform: Airtame 3, Airtame Go, Virtual Airtame, and browser, desktop, and mobile apps that go with them. The bar remains at an effortless experience. Someone walks into a room, and starts sharing. No app to hunt for, no login to chase.

The team is four engineers, and we're hiring their technical and people lead: someone who spends about 60% of time hands-on with the hardest problems, and the rest growing the engineers around them.

**About Airtame

**We're around 55 people, headquartered in Copenhagen, and you'd work from there or remotely from within the EU. We make the hardware and the software that runs on it, so a call you make about the streaming stack ends up in a product bolted to a wall in meeting rooms around the world. The team is small, works across disciplines, and reaches a global market from a small base.

Year one outcomes

Make joining a call one step that works. Today, getting an authenticated meeting started from a room takes too many turns: personal logins, manual entry, a different quirk on every platform. A year from now, starting a scheduled call on Teams, Zoom, Google Meet, or Webex should be something a room just does. Judge it by how often it works on the first try, and how rarely it reaches support.

Take the friction out of screen sharing. The browser path loses first-time users: too many clicks, not enough signposting. You'll own getting a newcomer from a short code to their screen on the wall without a stumble, and getting Miracast and AirPlay stable enough to turn on by default.

Make it behave the same everywhere. The experience varies between Airtame 3, Virtual Airtame, browser, desktop, and mobile today. By year-end, sharing and calling should feel like one product no matter which surface you're on, with real-time quality that holds up on whatever network the room happens to have.

Lead the team. You'll run the 1:1s, set the technical bar, and support team members' growth. The measure is simple: a year in, the team runs on your leadership day to day.

Push AI-assisted development further. The team already builds with AI daily. You'll lead the next step: sharper workflows, better tooling choices, new patterns that make the whole group faster. By year-end, the team's AI practices should be visibly ahead of where they started.

Who you are

• The player-coach. You've owned a team's technical direction: the architecture calls, the reviews where the hard problems get caught. And you want the people side too. Growing engineers, running 1:1s, hiring. You're not looking to trade one for the other. Maybe you've been a staff engineer or tech lead ready to own a team, or a manager who never stopped building. Either way, 60/40 sounds about right to you.

• Comfortable across the stack. Real-time media is second nature to you: WebRTC, streaming, the way audio and video behave over a network you don't control. You've gone deep somewhere, whether a media pipeline, native protocols, or a cross-platform client, and you can hold your own everywhere else, on browser, desktop, and mobile.

• You've made stubborn systems cooperate. Half this job is getting software to play nicely with platforms you don't own: Teams, Zoom, Meet, Webex, the operating system's own media APIs, each with its own idea of how things should go. You've done that kind of integration, and you keep your head when every platform behaves differently.

• You measure yourself by the room. Your bar is the person standing at the "share" button. Someone who's never seen an Airtame, getting their screen up first try with no help. That's what you optimize for, and it steers the calls you make when something has to give.

• You use AI as a daily tool. You write code with it, debug with it, prototype with it. You've formed your own view on where it speeds things up and where it gets in the way, and you help the people around you do the same.

****Why Airtame:

• The defining calls are still ahead. Airtame's collaboration software keeps spreading across more devices and form factors, so the shape of the next phase is still open, and you'd be the one setting it.

With an IoT platform connecting more than 6 million units — and growing — Trackunit is building the platform that will enable the construction industry to work faster, smarter, and more securely. And we need you to help run and scale it.

As an SRE, you will join our Europe-based team and be part of a global SRE organization spanning Europe and Canada. This is a hands-on role focused on the daily operation and continuous improvement of our platform, with room to grow into larger design and architecture work as you build depth.

The platform owned by SRE consists of an AWS cloud, Kubernetes clusters (EKS), and our IaC setup running Terraform and Terramate, as well as a GitOps delivery platform built on Argo CD and Atlantis.

We support engineering teams with 150+ developers. You will help keep a platform used by 15,000+ active users every day secure, available, and easy to build on.

We're looking for someone curious and collaborative — happy to share knowledge and ask questions as well.

Experience level: roughly 2–5 years in an SRE, DevOps, platform, or infrastructure operations role. If you're further along and the day-to-day scope appeals to you, apply anyway — we'll have the conversation.

With locations in the heart of Copenhagen, Kolding, Aarhus, and Aalborg, we offer a flexible setup with the possibility to work from one of our locations — or remotely from anywhere in Denmark.

**What's in it for you?

**

• International environment with regular check-ins and social events across teams, departments and borders.

• We take your personal and professional development goals seriously and we support them through training, coaching, and mindfulness as well as with an open feedback culture to enable you to identify your strengths and opportunities.

• Flexibility and hybrid working is not just a cliché to us or something we state in a job posting. We offer a flexible setup because we believe you know best how to structure your work. Once you have chosen how you work best, let us know what you need: we got you covered with the IT equipment you need for your work.

• Turning the Tide. At Trackunit, we aim to create and contribute to an inclusive workplace. And this priority starts with our hiring — we do not discriminate on the basis of gender identity, sexual orientation, personal expression, ethnicity, religious belief, or disability status. We only assess candidates on their qualifications and merit. Learn more about TIDE and other DE&I initiatives here.

**What You'll Do

**Your week will be a mix of keeping things running well and making them better.

• Operate and improve the platform. Monitoring, alerting, capacity, cost, and the steady stream of small improvements that keep a large AWS and Kubernetes estate healthy.

• Work in code, not consoles. Infrastructure changes go through Terraform and Helm, reviewed as pull requests and delivered through Atlantis and Argo CD.

• Keep the platform secure. Patching, vulnerability remediation, base image updates, and closing findings — a recurring, meaningful part of the job rather than a side task.

• Take part in incident response. You'll join our on-call rotation (SRE team, business hours) and contribute to incidents and follow-up work.

• Handle triage and requests from developer teams. Understanding what they need, unblocking them, and spotting when a repeated request could be automated.

**Who You Are

**We think you'll need

• Hands-on experience running workloads on AWS.

• Basic knowledge with Kubernetes.

• Basic knowledge about infrastructure as code, ideally Terraform.

• Comfortable with Git, Linux and Windows.

• Clear written communication — a lot of our work happens in tickets, PRs, and docs.

**Nice to have, not expected

**

• EKS specifically, or tooling like Karpenter, Argo CD, Atlantis, or Terramate.

• Observability tooling (Prometheus, Grafana, Sumo Logic, or similar).

• Scripting in Python or Go.

• Security or compliance work — vulnerability management, CIS benchmarks, certification programmes.

• Multi-region or multi-account AWS architecture.

**What Matters More Than The Checklist

**

• You’re curious and self-driven, while also knowing when to ask for help when needed.

• You finish things. Small, well-tested changes shipped consistently beat big ideas that stall.

• You care about the developers and customers using the platform, not just the platform itself.

On AI: experience with AI tooling is not a requirement. An interest in working with it is. We already use AI in our daily engineering work — including MCP servers and agents against our own platform — and we expect that to grow. We don’t expect you to have experience with this—but we do expect curiosity and a willingness to learn.

Don't meet every single requirement? No worries — this is what we're looking for ideally, but if you're excited about this role and your experience doesn't align perfectly with every qualification, we still encourage you to apply.

**How You'll Grow Here

**We hire at this level expecting you to move beyond it, and we've structured the team so that happens on purpose rather than by accident.

• A rotation model that protects your focus. The team splits between operational duty and project work, so you're not permanently interrupt-driven. You get real blocks of time to go deep on something.

• Mentorship that's built in. Senior colleagues review your PRs and pair with you on incidents. Asking questions is the expected behaviour, not a sign you're struggling.

• Exposure to the big architecture work. You'll start with scoped pieces and take on more as you build context.

• A clear conversation about your development. Regular 1:1s that cover where you want to be, not just what you shipped last sprint.

**What We're Building Next

**Trackunit is moving from a SaaS company to a platform built on telemetry data from the construction industry worldwide. For SRE, that means going beyond delivering infrastructure to building the capabilities that let our developers and customers spin up environments tailored to their needs in the regions they need them.

Things on our roadmap include:

• Expanding the platform into a true multi-region architecture.

• Building self-service platform capabilities so developer teams move at their own pace.

• Making better use of AI in our own operations, through MCP servers and agents.

You won't be expected to lead these on day one. You will be in the room, and there will be pieces with your name on them.

**What Happens From Here — Recruitment Process Overview

**

• Virtual meet and greet. Meet with a member of our Talent Partner team

• Personality-based interview. You will be asked to complete an online personality assessment prior to the interview. There are no correct answers and we are not trying to categorise you — the aim is a dialogue about the results and Trackunit's culture, so you get to know us better as well.

• Assignment-specific interview. You will be given a case to prepare after the initial screening interview. You will present the case to relevant colleagues across Trackunit, who you will also work closely with in the role.

• Virtual meet and greet. Meet with Engineering Manager, Kåre Brandborg and an SRE team member.

• References and background checks (if needed). If required, we will obtain references from former employers and perform level-specific background checks, if you have not provided these yourself.

• Offer presentation and walk-through. We're lucky to have you!

**Coming Together To Connect Construction

**We're committed to construction — one of the largest industries in the world. Over the past two decades, Trackunit has been pioneering technological progress within construction. Today, we are not only a leading IoT provider but a thought leader, supporting and shaping the agenda for an entire industry on a global scale.

We believe in taking a people approach in everything we do. Being human-centric is not restricted to our products — it's a way of life at Trackunit. We're proud to be a truly global team. Our colleagues get together in hubs spread across the globe, but we embrace the idea of working remotely and in environments that inspire you. Everything we do, we do it to eliminate downtime and build the most useful industry for the world.

The question is: Are you in?

jobs.occupation: Experienced Senior Lean Consultant for Project Excellence at Novo Nordisk Engineering
jobs.description:
If you’re energised by driving lean transformation at a company level and you thrive on turning complex challenges into tangible business impact, we’d love to hear from you!

Who we are

We are a leading pharma engineering company shaping the future of API pharma engineering globally. Leveraging the expertise of 2,000+ employees across Denmark, India, and the US, we design, build and optimise pharmaceutical manufacturing facilities that are essential to the health and well-being of patients everywhere.

Our success is driven by passion, innovation, and collaboration — with our customers and across our teams and disciplines. If you share our dedication to a noble cause and our passion for API pharma engineering, then NNE is the place for you.

About the role

We are looking for a Senior Lean Consultant to join our team of highly skilled colleagues in the Project Excellence department. In Project Excellence, we act as internal consultants grounded in Lean, supporting projects and leadership across NNE by strengthening performance management, structured problem solving and continuous improvement practices.

As a Senior Lean Consultant, you will work closely with project organisations and leaders to set direction for improvement initiatives, build Lean capabilities and drive performance. At the same time, you will take an active, hands-on role in facilitating problem solving and implementing improvements on our most critical projects, ensuring that ideas translate into real impact.

This role offers a unique opportunity to operate at the intersection of leadership, Lean transformation and project execution, contributing to building a strong and sustainable performance and improvement culture across NNE.

You’ll be based in our Virum Office, but the role requires you to visit our project sites in Kalundborg and around the Copenhagen area on a regular basis.

How you might spend your days

As a Senior Lean Consultant, you’ll be:

• Helping the Project Excellence department set direction for continuous improvement and Lean in NNE, aligned with NNE’s strategy

• Building Lean capabilities by developing and embedding structured problem solving, lean project management and continuous improvement practices

• Designing and delivering training in Lean tools, Lean principles and Lean ways of working across NNE

• Coaching leaders and teams to strengthen performance management and Lean leadership behaviours

• Facilitating and driving structured problem-solving on major projects, using A3 thinking as our core approach

• Advising on consistent implementation of improvements, ensuring solutions are anchored and deliver real impact

Who you are

We care about who you are as a person. In the end, how you work, and your energy is what impacts the results we achieve as a team. As a person, you are:

• Passionate about Lean thinking and driven to create real lasting business impact

• Confident in engaging, challenging and developing leaders and teams at all levels

• Comfortable operating in complex environments, bringing clarity, structure and direction

• Pragmatic and execution-focused with a great drive to turn ideas into results

• A credible role model who takes ownership and leads by example

What you bring to the role

In all positions, there are some things that are preferred, and others, a bonus. If you do not meet all the qualifications listed below, you are welcome to offer alternative experience that you think would be valuable in this role:

• Extensive experience driving continuous improvement and lean transformations in complex organisations

• Proven ability to lead and implement change with measurable impact

• Solid experience working closely with senior leaders on performance and improvement agendas

• A relevant academic degree at Master level

• Excellent facilitation, coaching and stakeholder management skills across organisational levels

Life at NNE

NNE is short for Novo Nordisk Engineering. And for all of us who work here, NNE means so much more.

At NNE, you become part of a vibrant, project-based environment built on close day-to-day collaboration. Are you approaching the end of your studies and looking for a graduation project early 2027. Does deep dive into the protection of the primary equipment enabling transport of wind energy to shore excite you? Then we have the project for you.

The projects

Protection study

Today we apply state of the art, cutting edge protections of the primary equipment, 220/66kV transformers, shunt reactors, subsea cables etc. Functions like line differential protection, restricted earth fault protection, distance protection with fiber optic accelerations schemes and different mechanical protections.

But how well do the different protections cover the primary equipment?

Are all protections feasible, considering how often we statistically experience faults?

Grounding

Today the MV grid, connecting the wind turbines to the Offshore Sub Station is impedance grounded. This creates different problems and side effects that needs to be considered during engineering. Some primary equipment becomes expensive and hard to procure. Protection against earth faults becomes challenging because of the reduced fault current.

Investigate the benefits and disadvantages of isolated, impedance and effectively grounded MV grid.

How will the protections need to be set up?

What will the implications be on primary equipment, transformers, cables, wind turbines etc.
